question.text: An intermediary receives a complaint from an investor. Under the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008, what is the maximum time within which the complaint must be redressed?

answer.text: Not later than 45 days from receipt

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations require an intermediary to redress investor grievances promptly but not later than forty-five days from receipt of the complaint. The Trap: 30 days is a commonly assumed grievance-redressal period under other frameworks and is the most attractive distractor, but the source-backed period under these regulations is 45 days. Note: Asking for the time limit, rather than an exact calendar date, avoids ambiguity about leap years and date-counting conventions (e.g. whether the date of receipt is included).
